input.title: CM-01: PR #2 merged to main without independent approval
input.body:
**PR #2 was merged into `main` without approval from anyone other than the author (2 commits).**

**Guardrails:** P1–P6 all **pass** (PR required, 1 approval, stale approvals dismissed, `test` required, no bypass actors, force-push and deletion blocked). I didn't change the ruleset, so I didn't run verify_repo.

**What happened:** D1 (all changes came through PRs) and D3 (`test` passed) both pass. D2 **fails** because nobody independently approved PR #2:
- `599d9a1` merge of PR #2 (TheEraptic, 2026-10-07) → retro review: https://github.com/TheEraptic/grc-lab-payments-api/issues/5
- `46d465d` "docs: add test instructions to README" (claude, 2026-10-07) → retro review: https://github.com/TheEraptic/grc-lab-payments-api/issues/6

Both issues were **already open** from an earlier run, so I didn't create duplicates.

**What you need to do:** Have someone other than the author review both commits and record the result in #5 and #6. The ruleset requires 1 approval, but the merge still went through. Please check whether the approval came from a bot or AI account, or whether the author was able to approve their own PR.

The repo is classified as production. Apart from completing the reviews, you don't need to reply unless you disagree.

All the guardrail checks (P1–P6) and the other history checks (D1, D3) passed. Because none of P1–P6 failed, I didn't change the ruleset or run `verify_repo`.

I tried to open a retro-review issue for each of the two commits, `599d9a1` and `46d465d`. Both issues were already open from an earlier run, so no duplicates were created: [#5](https://github.com/TheEraptic/grc-lab-payments-api/issues/5) and [#6](https://github.com/TheEraptic/grc-lab-payments-api/issues/6).

I sent the owner one notification marked "action_required" because the two retro reviews still need to be done. It went in as a [comment on existing alert #5](https://github.com/TheEraptic/GRC-Engineering/issues/5#issuecomment-6135419980) in the control repo. In it, I asked them to check how PR #2 got merged when the ruleset requires an approval. That's my guess, not something I confirmed: the approval may have come from a bot or AI account, or the author may have approved it themselves.
